Updated hypothesis:

1. Since Vision Zero began, the number of pedestrians and cyclists killed or seriously injured (KSI) has not declined significantly.


2. Among reported pedestrian and cyclist crashes, was the proportion involving serious or fatal injuries higher on state-maintained routes than on county routes?


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
```


```{r}
nonmotorists <- read_csv("https://data.montgomerycountymd.gov/api/v3/views/n7fk-dce5/query.csv") |>
  clean_names()

```


Years in the dataset:
```{r}
nonmotorists <- nonmotorists |>
  mutate(year = year(crash_date_time))

nonmotorists |> count(year)
```

Injury categories:

```{r}
nonmotorists |> count(injury_severity)
```
Type of road each crash is on:
```{r}
nonmotorists |> count(route_type, sort = TRUE)
```

Number of people killed/seriously injured (KSI):

```{r}
ksi_by_year <- nonmotorists |>
  filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(injury_severity), "fatal|serious"), year <= 2025) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(ksi_people = n())

ksi_by_year

ksi_by_year |> summarise(average = mean(ksi_people))
```


Line chart:

```{r}
ksi_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = ksi_people)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Pedestrians and cyclists killed or seriously injured",
    subtitle = "Montgomery County, MD -- 2015–2025",
    x = "Year",
    y = "People killed or seriously injured (KSI)",
    caption = "Source: Montgomery County crash reporting data (DataMontgomery)")

```

# of People Killed/Seriously Injured Each Year:

```{r}
ksi_by_year <- nonmotorists |>
  filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(injury_severity), "fatal|serious"), year <= 2025) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(ksi_people = n_distinct(person_id))
```

Results:

2015	92
2016	75
2017	90
2018	88
2019	97
2020	64
2021	64
2022	105
2023	79
2024	89
2025	98

These show me that the year that had the most people killed/seriously injured was 2022.  


Regression (based on HW13):

```{r}
ksi_model <- lm(ksi_people ~ year, data = ksi_by_year)
summary(ksi_model)

```
This tells me that my Adjusted R-squared is -0.09499. My p-value is 0.7242. The coefficient for year is 0.4909.


Scatterplot:


```{r}
ksi_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = ksi_people)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  labs(
    title = "Pedestrians and cyclists killed or seriously injured, by year",
    subtitle = "Montgomery County, MD, 2015–2025",
    x = "Year",
    y = "People killed or seriously injured (KSI)",
    caption = "Source: Montgomery County crash reporting data (dataMontgomery)"
    
  )
```

The trend line on the scatterplot slope upward, starting at about 83 in 2015 to about 88 by 2025. The dots are scattered far from the line, which is reflected in the low R-squared and the p-value above 0.05. It's also worth noting that the pandemic years in 2020 and 2021 are the lowest on the chart, likely because of less cars on the roads.

This data overall shows that even though the slope is positive, there's no evidence of any real trend because of the adusted R-squared value. This supports my first hypothesis that people killed or seriously injured has NOT gone down since Vision Zero began.


Check on Hypothesis #1:

Code from Derek (from 11/19 feedback)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

nonmotorist_crashes <- nonmotorists |>
  mutate(
    ksi_person = case_when(
      is.na(injury_severity) |
        str_trim(injury_severity) == "" |
        str_detect(
          str_to_lower(injury_severity),
          "unknown|not reported"
        ) ~ NA,

      TRUE ~ str_detect(
        str_to_lower(injury_severity),
        "fatal|serious"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(report_number) |>
  summarize(
    year = first(year),
    route_type = first(route_type),
    nonmotorists_involved = n(),

    ksi_crash = case_when(
      any(ksi_person %in% TRUE) ~ TRUE,
      any(is.na(ksi_person)) ~ NA,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

The above code from Derek allowed me to have one row per crash, so crashes involving several people aren't counted repeatedly.


How to count crashes (with help from AI:)
```{r}
ksi_crashes_by_year <- nonmotorist_crashes |>
  filter(ksi_crash %in% TRUE, year <= 2025) |>
  count(year, name = "ksi_crashes")

ksi_crashes_by_year

ksi_crashes_by_year |> summarise(average = mean(ksi_crashes))
```
This shows me that the average number of KSI crashes per year is 84.


Regression on crashes:

```{r}
crash_model <- lm(ksi_crashes ~ year, data = ksi_crashes_by_year)
summary(crash_model)
```
This tells me my p-value is 0.6843, my adjusted R-squared is -0.08975, and my years coefficient is 0.5273.

Scatterplot:

```{r}
ggplot(ksi_crashes_by_year, aes(x = year, y = ksi_crashes)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(ksi_crashes_by_year$year)) +
  labs(x = "Year",
    y = "KSI crashes",
    title = "Crashes killing or seriously injuring a pedestrian or cyclist",
    caption = "Source: Montgomery County crash reporting data (dataMontgomery)")
```
This shows me that there is an  upward trend in the number of KSI crashes per year, from about 81 in 2015 to about 86 in 2025. The years are widely scattered, so the line doesn't explain much. Just like the other scatterplot, 2020 and 2021 are the lowest values, and then 2022 is one of the highest years.

Question: "Is Vision Zero reducing the number of pedestrians and cyclists killed or seriously injured in Montgomery County?"

Hypothesis:

1. Since Vision Zero began, the number of pedestrians and cyclists killed or seriously injured has NOT declined significantly.
2. **NEW***: Among reported pedestrian and cyclist crashes, was the proportion involving serious or fatal injuries higher on state routes than on county routes?



```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

Here is the nonmotorist data:

THIS DATA COVERS:

This is data from the Montgomery County Government that shows individual records of nonmotorist crashes in Montgomery County (one row per person). It is updated weekly by the county, but I will only use full calendar years of data (January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2025. All these crashes come from police reports that are filed through the Automated Crash Reporting System (ACRS). 

Format: CSV


Most important columns: date, non-motorist type, route type, road name, injury severity
What's missing: Data for crashes on interstates and the ICC (Maryland Route 200), High Injury Network and project maps



```{r}

nonmotorists <- read_csv ("https://data.montgomerycountymd.gov/api/views/n7fk-dce5/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD")

```

Here is the incidents dataset:


This table has one row per every crash: every traffic collision reported on local and county roads in Montgomery County, NOT JUST ones involving cyclists or pedestrians. Data runs from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2025 (will only use full years of data).

Format: CSV

```{r}
incidents <- read_csv ("https://data.montgomerycountymd.gov/api/views/bhju-22kf/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD")
```
